chief_complaint: A 5-day history of a febrile illness with fever and shock.
history_of_present_illness: The illness started with a sore throat, aching all over, abdominal pain, and diarrhoea, with the patient becoming increasingly unwell and weak.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Her husband, who worked in a local gold mine, died 6 days before her illness from a severe febrile illness, and she had cared for him.
vitals: Blood pressure 85/65 mmHg, pulse rate 105 bpm, temperature 38°C (100.4°F).
physical_exam: Looks very unwell, has bilateral conjunctivitis, no rash or lymphadenopathy, normal heart sounds, clear chest, and normal abdominal examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Malaria slide showed a low level of Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia, and a positive Marburg virus PCR result was confirmed post-discharge.
differential_diagnosis: Malaria, typhoid fever, bacterial sepsis (including meningococcal disease), severe viral infections (adenovirus, influenza), measles, Zika virus, and viral haemorrhagic fever (VHF) such as Marburg virus disease.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was isolated and treated with IV artesunate, artemether/lumefantrine, empirical IV ceftriaxone, and IV fluids, improving after several days and discharged after 2 additional days in isolation.
